To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
Aβ impairs memory consolidation by compromising synaptic remodeling and that this occurs very early in the formation of long-term memories.

1) Aβ impairs the consolidation of memory; 2) Aβ-mediated impairment is highly dependent on time interval between training and injection; 3) Aβ-mediated memory impairment is associated with lower density and altered structure of synapses in the dentate and CA1 fields of the hippocampus.
human brain-derived amyloid-β protein impairs consolidation of avoidance memory in the rat by compromising the structural synaptic plasticity essential for memory formation.
